quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does smooth downshifting do on a motorcycle?

options.text: It lets the engine help slow the motorcycle.
You should not do it when other vehicles are nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets the engine help slow the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Engine braking through smooth downshifting is useful for motorcycle riders. If you use engine braking, use your brake lights separately so other drivers know you are slowing down.

questions.question: What material are riding gloves usually made from?
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually made of leather. Gloves improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: When should a rider check their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down or stopping, at intersections, when changing lanes, and when turning.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing that covers your body. This includes sturdy pants and jackets that cover your arms and legs, boots that cover and support your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to ride next to a car?

options.text: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
It is only a problem when the road is wet.
It makes driving easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous. The driver may not see you in their blind spot. The vehicle also blocks your escape route.

questions.question: Which surface is slippery and hard to control a motorcycle on?
questions.explanation: Wet roads, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal covers in the road are all slippery. Ride with extra care on these surfaces.

questions.question: What best reduces head and neck injuries?
questions.explanation: A high-quality helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries. It is your best protection in a crash.

questions.question: How can you be more visible to other drivers?
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen during the day. Always wear bright clothing while riding, even during daylight hours.

questions.question: What should motorcycle riding clothing cover?

options.text: Your arms completely, but not your legs
Your legs completely, but not your arms
Whatever feels comfortable, regardless of safety

questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs for proper protection.

questions.question: What should you think about when choosing your lane position?

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you
Which position makes your trip shorter
Which position lets you pass more vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that makes sure other drivers can see you and that gives you enough space to stop or maneuver.

questions.question: Regular maintenance on your motorcycle helps because:

options.text: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
Maintenance checks take a lot of time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle will stay in good condition if you maintain it properly and perform regular inspections.

questions.question: If your shoes have laces, you should:
questions.explanation: Tuck your shoelaces in securely while riding so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: Motorcycles:

options.text: Do not have blind spots because they are small.
Have blind spots, but they are small enough not to worry about.
Have blind spots that you should check regularly.
Are too small to have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that you should check regularly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your regular scanning.

questions.question: When choosing footwear for riding, pick:

options.text: Shoes with long laces that can't be tucked in.

questions.explanation: Wear boots or shoes that are tall and strong enough to cover and support your ankles. Heels should be short so they don't catch on things. Tuck laces in so they can't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator?
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handlegrip and you control it with your right hand.

questions.question: To check tire pressure, you should:

options.text: Look at the tire to estimate pressure.
Squeeze the tire with your hand.
Compare it to another tire's height.

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check pressure before every ride. A tire that looks fine may still be under-inflated, so looking alone is not enough.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually found?
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handlegrip. Know where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: A motorcycle needs:

options.text: Less regular attention than a car.
More regular attention than a car.
Checks only by a mechanic before each ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: More regular attention than a car.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle more often than a car. Do a full check before every ride.

questions.question: Low-speed crashes:

options.text: Happen often, so don't worry about them.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds under 30 miles per hour. Even crashes at low speeds can be fatal.

questions.question: Riding at night:

options.text: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
Is not safe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.
Should only be done in the city.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective clothing when riding at night. This makes other drivers able to see you better.

questions.question: When riding, keeping space around your motorcycle helps you:

options.text: React quickly if something goes wrong.
Avoid being able to escape danger.

questions.correctAnswerText: React quickly if something goes wrong.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle at all times. This gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You need this space to move safely.

questions.question: For motorcycle safety, you should:

options.text: Assume everything on your motorcycle works properly.
Check your motorcycle before every ride.
Check your motorcycle once a month.
Check your motorcycle twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle carefully before every ride.

questions.question: What can help other drivers see you at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to get attention.

questions.explanation: Use your headlight at intersections and ride in a position where oncoming traffic can see you. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can escape danger if needed.

questions.question: You should not ride directly beside another vehicle because:

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may want to use the lane.
It would be hard to see what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding beside another vehicle is dangerous. The driver may not see you in their blind spot. Also, the vehicle could block your way to escape if danger appears.
